about.title: What it does
body: ML Toolkit is a small workbench for preparing audio datasets. Pick a tool, upload a file and download the result. It is made for the datasets behind AI music detection.

Conversion moves a file between WAV, MP3, FLAC and OGG, with a bitrate choice for the lossy formats. Augmentation makes new samples from an existing one: pitch shift, speed change, bass boost, silence trimming, mixing and added noise. Dataset organization reads a file and reports its duration, tempo, key and loudness, so a folder can be labelled without opening each track.
Processing runs on the CrownCode backend. If it has been idle it needs a minute or two to wake up, and the first request waits for it.

faq.title: Questions people ask
faq.lead: Most visitors arrive with one of these.

items.q: How can you tell if a song was made with AI?
items.a: There are a few things to listen for: vocals that never take a breath, lyrics that drift off meaning, a texture that stays the same from start to finish, endings that stop for no reason. People's songs can have all of these too. AURIS takes 47 measurements from the audio, feeds them to a model trained on 5,195 labelled songs, and shows which measurement pushed the result which way.

items.q: Does it recognise songs made with Suno or Udio?
items.a: The training set includes tracks made with Suno, Udio, MusicGen, AudioLDM, ACE-Step and DiffRhythm. New versions of these tools can fool it, so read the result as a likelihood, not a ruling.

In cross-validation it is 88.4% accurate with a ROC-AUC of 0.955, so roughly one song in nine is misclassified. The closer the probability is to the threshold (0.432), the less certain the result; the report shows this on the Certainty line.

items.q: Can it show which part of a song is AI?
items.a: It shows where the song reads AI-like. The track (up to the first six minutes) is read in windows of about 30 seconds, and each window gets its own probability, drawn under the waveform. The model was trained on whole tracks that were either all AI or all human-made, so a high window means that stretch sounds like AI music, not that an AI was used only there. A mixed track, such as a human song with an AI-made intro, can show up as a change along the timeline, but treat it as a hint.

Not on the server: the file is dropped from memory once the analysis ends, and only the result is kept for a few hours in case the same file comes back. The last audio stays in your own browser so a reload can pick up where it left off. For the FST layer, a copy goes to the mippia team's Hugging Face Space.

items.q: Is it free? Do I need an account?
items.a: It's free and there's no account. Files can be up to 30 MB. The server runs one analysis at a time, so at busy moments you wait in line, and the page shows your place.

items.q: How does a YouTube link work?
items.a: The server downloads the audio of the first six minutes and analyses it the same way as a file. YouTube blocks downloads for some videos; if that happens, upload the song as a file.

method.title: Model and validation
method.lead: LightGBM: {samples} tracks ({ai} AI-generated, {human} human-made), {features} features. Metrics use {folds}-fold cross-validation. Model files are public on Hugging Face.
method.step1: 47 features are extracted from the opening 60 seconds. The rest of the track, up to six minutes, is then read in windows of about 30 seconds.
method.step2: LightGBM estimates the probability for the opening; values above {t} are assigned to the AI class. The same model scores each window of the timeline.
method.step3: Predictions from 10 additional models are compared. SHAP computes feature contributions to the primary prediction.
method.step4: wav2vec2, FST and vocal analysis results are reported separately.
method.limit1: Performance may drop on genres and generators absent from the training data.
method.limit2: Heavy processing, electronic music, microphone recordings and low audio quality can cause misclassification.
method.limit3: Cross-validation accuracy: {acc}%. This does not guarantee performance on new tracks or prove their origin.
method.limit4: Timeline windows are about 30 seconds long, shorter than the 60-second clips the model was trained on, and each training clip was either all AI or all human-made. A window shows where the music reads AI-like, not where an AI was used.

about.title: What this is
body: Crown Fortune is a small daily ritual. Once a day you spin the wheel and it settles on one of five areas: love, career, wealth, vitality or spirit. A card from a 22-card deck is drawn for it, along with a short message, lucky numbers, a lucky colour and the current moon phase.

meta.title: Privacy Policy | CrownCode
meta.description: What data CrownCode collects, how it is used and how it is protected.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page says what the CrownCode site and its tools do with your data.

dataCollection.title: What is collected
dataCollection.content: There are no accounts. On a sample of visits the site records anonymous page-speed measurements and the page they came from. The servers that host the site and the tools (Cloudflare and Hugging Face) keep ordinary access logs, which can include your IP address and browser.

dataUsage.title: What happens to what you send
dataUsage.content: Audio, a dream text or a video link goes to the tool's server only to produce your result. Analyses are held in memory for a short while so you can fetch the result, then discarded. Crown Dreams sends the dream text, and Crown Commend the video's transcript, to Google's Gemini API to write the reply; Google handles that text under its own terms. Nothing is sold or used for advertising.

dataSecurity.title: On your device
dataSecurity.content: Your language choice, your analysis history and your Crown Fortune draws are kept in your browser's local storage and never leave your device. Clear the site's data in your browser to remove them. Traffic between you and the site is encrypted over HTTPS.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.content: One cookie remembers your language. There are no tracking or advertising cookies.

Hosted web demos (such as AURIS audio detection, Creator Studio mixing, Crown Dreams and Crown Commend) run as research projects and can change, rate-limit or go offline without notice. Standalone open-source tools such as FL-MCP and VOTRYX execute locally on your own hardware.

userResponsibilities.title: Your responsibility
userResponsibilities.content: Do not use the tools for spam, automated abuse, or anything that breaks the terms of another service such as YouTube. Text or MIDI patterns generated by AI or algorithmic helpers are drafts, and you are responsible for reviewing what you publish online or send to a live DAW project. Upload only audio files you have the right to process.

intellectualProperty.title: Ownership
intellectualProperty.content: The site and its content belong to Hasan Arthur Altuntaş. Source code is published under the licence stated in each repository, mostly MIT. Audio, MIDI, project files and text you provide stay yours; local tools do not transmit FL Studio projects to CrownCode servers.

disclaimer.title: No warranty
disclaimer.content: Everything is provided as it is, without warranty. Hosted analysis models and AI outputs can make mistakes, so do not base clinical, legal or commercial decisions solely on automated scores. Temporary interruptions, ephemeral job expiry and third-party API availability (such as Google Gemini or YouTube) are outside CrownCode's control.

creatorStudio.title: Creator Studio
creatorStudio.subtitle: Tools for remixing and mixing tracks

about.title: How the tools work
body: Remix Studio takes two tracks, detects the tempo and key of each, stretches and pitch-shifts the second one to fit the first, and joins them with a crossfade you set. The result downloads as a WAV file.
The Multi-Track Mixer takes two to six tracks. You set each track's level and its place between left and right, and the mix is bounced to one file with its peak level normalised so it does not clip.
Each file can be up to 30 MB. Processing runs on the CrownCode backend, so the first request after a quiet spell can take a minute or two.

specs.label: Supported formats
specs.value: Accepts WAV, MP3, FLAC and OGG audio files up to 30 MB per uploaded stem or track.

specs.label: Tempo & key matching
specs.value: Estimates BPM and Chroma pitch profile, then applies phase-vocoder time-stretching and pitch shifting.

specs.label: Multitrack routing
specs.value: Combines 2 to 6 tracks with independent fader gain and constant-power stereo left-right panning.

specs.label: Peak-safe export
specs.value: Normalizes the bounced stereo mix to -1 dBFS and exports uncompressed PCM WAV output.

transparency.title: Architecture Transparency
transparency.subtitle: Where FL Studio's Scripting API stops, and the 5-layer resolution ladder FL-MCP uses without breaking stability or focus.
transparency.intro: Image-Line's official Python Scripting API intentionally blocks offline bounce rendering, direct binary .flp/.fst inspection and certain third-party modal dialogs. Rather than claiming magic capabilities, FL-MCP separates each task onto the lightest reliable engineering layer.

layers.scope: Transport, BPM, Mixer inserts, FX routing view="io", VST parameters
layers.how: Direct bidirectional MIDI CC + SysEx bridge over loopMIDI (Windows), IAC Driver (macOS) or Wine (Linux) with deterministic fl_param unit conversion.
layers.boundary: Primary fast path. Cannot bounce audio files offline or insert arbitrary score blocks directly into arbitrary Piano Roll positions.

layers.scope: Named chords (Am7@0:4, Fmaj7@4:4), Piano Roll queueing, preview=true
layers.how: Bridges FL Piano Roll script helpers and live transport monitoring with tolerant float (0-1) or MIDI integer velocity.
layers.boundary: Requires controller port binding once via 1-click installer in FL-MCP Studio or script folder copy.

layers.scope: Full project assembly (fl_produce) and acoustic sample library ranking (fl_library)
layers.how: Reads and writes binary .flp structures, injects .fst presets and .sf2 SoundFonts, and analyzes local sample folders by brightness, decay and sub weight.
layers.boundary: Produces clean standalone or template-overlay .flp project files on disk without interrupting active playback.

layers.scope: Closed-loop BS.1770-4 / EBU 3342 mastering and objective mix verification
layers.how: Runs parallel FL64.exe /R CLI bounces inside an isolated hidden Windows desktop so FL Studio never steals keyboard or mouse focus during iterative limiter gain convergence.
layers.boundary: Parallel hidden desktop bounce requires Windows FL64.exe; macOS and Linux still run full live API, .flp file assembly and fl_audio WAV measurement.

layers.scope: Unscriptable VST buttons, export dialogs and legacy browser menus
layers.how: Off by default. In stealth mode captures via PrintWindow and dispatches PostMessageW without moving your cursor; polite mode waits for user idle and restores focus.
layers.boundary: Explicit opt-in only, protected at all times by moving the mouse to (0,0) top-left screen corner as an immediate fail-safe stop.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Engineering facts about live testing, platform compatibility, privacy and Scripting API boundaries.

items.q: Has FL-MCP been tested against a real FL Studio installation or only mocks?
items.a: Both. Live integration was verified on Windows 11 against real FL Studio 2025 (Producer Edition v25.2.5 [build 5319], Scripting API 40) where all 17 deep checks in fl-mcp selftest --deep pass. In addition, an 894-test offline CI suite covers official fl-studio-api-stubs, loopback MIDI, .flp binary parsing/writing, BS.1770-4 reference audio, HTTP/SSE transport and the desktop app.

items.q: Do I need Python or terminal experience to use FL-MCP?
items.a: No. Starting in v0.3.0, FL-MCP Studio ships as self-contained desktop archives for Windows, macOS and Linux with 1-click FL Studio controller script installation, 1-click AI client registration, live Transport/Mixer/Step Sequencer controls and MIDI TX/RX inspection.

items.q: Why does FL-MCP emphasize 14 flat-schema tools around ~4k tokens?
items.a: Many MCP servers emit deeply nested JSON schemas with $ref, anyOf and title metadata that bloat prompt context or break tool calling on smaller and local LLMs. Keeping 14 flat-schema tools under ~4k tokens leaves room for musical context and improves parameter accuracy.

items.q: Does hidden rendering or fl_desk steal my mouse focus while working?
items.a: Hidden mastering renders use parallel FL64.exe /R execution inside a separate hidden Windows desktop so focus stays with your foreground window. Optional fl_desk defaults to off; when enabled in stealth mode it captures windows with PrintWindow and sends inputs via PostMessageW without stealing focus, plus a (0,0) top-left screen corner failsafe stops automation instantly.

items.q: What platforms and AI clients are supported in v0.3.0?
items.a: Platforms: Windows x86_64 and ARM64 via loopMIDI, macOS Apple Silicon arm64 and Intel x86_64 via IAC Driver, and Linux x86_64 and ARM64 with Wine path resolution. Clients: Claude Desktop (.mcpb), Claude Code plugin (/plugin marketplace add Rtur2003/FL-MCP), Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and Codex CLI over stdio, Streamable-HTTP (:8765/mcp) or SSE (/sse).

items.q: Are my audio files, stems or .flp projects uploaded anywhere?
items.a: Never. Audio rendering, ITU-R BS.1770-4 metering, .flp generation, MIDI loopback and sample analysis execute 100% locally. Open-source builds from GitHub are completely unmetered and make zero backend calls.
